data.title: European Shares Poised To Open Higher
data.description:
BRUSSELS/FRANKFURT/PARIS (dpa-AFX) - European stocks are set to open on a firm note on Friday despite long-term anxieties surrounding the AI trade, lingering Middle East tensions and expectations for higher-for-longer interest rates.

Global technology stocks stabilized after recent string of losses due to dip-buying.

Amid tighter U.S. export controls, Nvidia is not allowing orders of computer servers containing its artificial intelligence chips to be shipped to four Southeast Asian countries, the Financial Times reported Thursday.

On the geopolitical front, a strike on an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia's southern Jazan region heightened concerns over supply disruptions from the Middle East.

Earlier, there was an attack on the Ras Tanura oil hub in the Persian Gulf, and a tanker was hit in the Strait of Hormuz.

Two Italian nationals were killed on Thursday in a drone attack on the Gulf nation of Kuwait. Clarifying that it had no involvement in the incident, Tehran warned against attempts to widen confrontations.

Separately, Israel said it is ready to strike Iran 'at any moment' even without U.S. military involvement, heightening concerns over a potential escalation of the conflict in the region.

Late Thursday, U.S. President Donald Trump said on PBS that the United States has 'victory at hand' in the Iran conflict, while expressing uncertainty over whether Iran would accept the opportunity for a deal.

Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghci said that Tehran's immediate focus was on strengthening the country's resilience against the pressures that enemies apply through various means.

Closer home, Spain goes to the polls on Sunday in an early parliamentary election.

Latest polls put the conservative Popular Party ahead of incumbent PM Pedro Sanchez's Socialists.

Spanish central banking veteran Pablo Hernandez de Cos has been chosen to succeed Christine Lagarde as the next European Central Bank President.

U.S. stock futures ticked higher ahead of a shortened Wall Street session following the Thanksgiving holiday.

Asian markets were mostly higher amid easing concerns over U.S. trade tensions.

Treasuries fell, with yield on the benchmark 10-year note rising two basis points to 4.87 percent as trading resumed after the Thanksgiving holiday. The U.S. dollar hovered below a 22-month peak as AI worries eased.

Gold jumped more than 2 percent to $3,651 on ounce after sinking to a 15-month low earlier in the week. Amid persistent inflation and growing volatility, investors looked ahead to next month's Federal Reserve meeting for signals on the path of borrowing costs.

Brent crude futures surged toward $97 a barrel and were on track for their first weekly gain this month following recent attacks on Middle eastern energy facilities and tankers.

On Thursday, European stocks staged a broad-based rally amid signs that Washington would respect the 15 percent levy the European Union had concluded with the United States.

The pan-European STOXX 600 jumped 1.8 percent after falling 1.1 percent on Wednesday.

The German DAX rallied 2.1 percent, France's CAC 40 gained 1.6 percent and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 surged 1.8 percent.

data.title: Ventura Offshore Holding Ltd.: Third Quarter 2026 Results
data.description:
November 27, 2026 - Ventura Offshore Holding Ltd. (the “Company”) announces results for the third quarter of 2026. The results highlights will be discussed in an audio conference call on Friday, November 27, 2026 at 14:00 CET. Dial-in details for the conference call can be found below.

Highlights

  • Quarterly operational uptime of 98% and financial uptime of 93.9% for the combined fleet of owned and managed rigs
  • Net loss of $12.6 million for the quarter
  • Adjusted EBITDA of $2.1 million for the quarter
  • Free cash position of $91.5 million
  • SSV Victoria and DS Carolina completed drilling contracts and commenced SPS and project phase
  • Announced exercise of 4th optional well and award of an additional 5th well for SSV Catarina
  • Announced marketing and operations agreement for Deep Value Driller followed by a drilling contract with Petronas in Indonesia
  • Announced Letter of Intent for an all-share combination with SED Energy Holdings Plc

Subsequent events

  • Raised new bridge loan financing of $250 million
  • Repaid outstanding bond loan of $190 million

Guilherme Coelho, Chief Executive Officer, commented:

“We are happy to report another operationally and commercially strong quarter. Our teams again delivered 98% operational uptime across the fleet. Additional wells for SSV Catarina with Eni in Indonesia were secured and we signed marketing and management contracts for the Deep Value Driller drillship, followed by a drilling contract with Petronas in Indonesia. We also announced a Letter of Intent for a combination with SED Energy Holdings to create a larger, more diversified offshore services platform.

We are progressing well on the ongoing special periodic surveys and preparation work for our SSV Victoria and DS Carolina ahead of their upcoming long-term contracts with Petrobras, expected to commence in early 2027. Since quarter end, we have strengthened our balance sheet by raising a $250 million bridge loan financing on favourable terms and repaying the outstanding bond loan of $190 million, providing the Company with liquidity to fully fund its ongoing upgrade and maintenance requirements. Together, these are important steps towards creating sustainable, long-term value for our employees, customers and shareholders.”

data.title: Sanofi CEO got to work on $41 billion Insmed deal straight after taking office
data.description:
Key points:
  • Sanofi share price has gained 26% since Garijo became CEO
  • Initially investors were cautious after her record at Merck
  • Garijo says she still has much work to do

By Dominique Patton and Bhanvi Satija

Sanofi CEO Belen Garijo began working on what became a $41 billion takeover of US biotech Insmed as soon as she started her job in May, she told Reuters, explaining how she struck Sanofi's biggest deal in 20 years.

The deal has boosted the French pharmaceuticals company's share price to its highest in more than a year and investors have said it could buy time to strengthen the drug pipeline and lessen reliance on top-selling eczema drug Dupixent.

In her first comments on how the deal came about, Garijo told Reuters she had thought of the deal "immediately after I arrived, with a new team".

"We did a lot of work internally on our side before engaging with them," she added, speaking on the sidelines of the Economy Summit conference in Paris.

Garijo, who was brought in from Germany's Merck KGaA to turn around Sanofi's fortunes and fix its pipeline, said the team did deep diligence and analysis on Insmed's data and business case before discussing it with the board.

"We needed the strong support from the very beginning from our board and that was the case because it was a perfect fit," she said. "We had very constructive debates with the board until we could move."

INVESTORS WERE INITIALLY CAUTIOUS ABOUT GARIJO

When Sanofi's board picked Garijo as CEO in February, investors had greeted the choice with caution. During her previous tenure at Merck KGaA, she delivered mixed results on R&D and the share price fell.

However, investors said that in less than seven months at Sanofi, Garijo has convinced those who doubted her.

The Insmed deal dwarfs the $3.9 billion SpringWorks purchase that was among her biggest deals at Germany's Merck.

"I think she has probably surprised some investors," said Claus Henrik Johansen, CEO of Global Health Invest, a Danish healthcare investment fund which holds Sanofi shares.

"Every time a CEO steps into the office, we need to see actions to prioritise and set a direction for the company. I think Belen has done that."

Beyond the deal, which is expected to close next year, Garijo has hired a new R&D chief Paulo Fontoura, stopped development of certain drugs at Sanofi and smoothed relations with long-term partner Regeneron with an expanded deal worth $8 billion.

That has helped to dispel any "negative view", Jefferies analyst Michael Leuchten told Reuters, adding she had sealed a transformative deal in a short time, something that the previous CEO had not achieved in more than six years in the job.

"You've got a management team here that she's leading that is doing things now and gets board sign-off when the prior management team was not able to do that," Leuchten said.

Sanofi's stock has gained 13% in the last week and is up 26% since she took over in May.

The Insmed deal comes with some risks, including how quickly its lead drug Brinsupri is taken up, questions over pricing and launches of the drug outside the US next year, as well as competition from Boehringer Ingelheim's rival experimental drug.

Garijo said the deal addressed Sanofi's challenges, but she would not lower her guard.

"This has significantly improved our outlook and of course it has accelerated our pipeline, but we need to continue, the work is not over," she said. "The markets like it... but you can never let (your) guard down."

data.title: Poland's Russia-friendly party creates conundrum for conservatives ahead of 2027 vote
data.description:
Key points:
  • Polish right more divided than in previous election cycles
  • Right-wing parties' combined vote share gives them chance of forming government
  • Russia-friendly KKP party increases in popularity
  • Party's rise creates difficult choices for conservatives

By Alicja Surdy and Alan Charlish

Poland's fragmented right wing is seeking common ground to try to unseat centrist Prime Minister Donald Tusk in 2027 elections, with some leaders making overtures to a Russia-friendly party that is an anathema to many traditional conservatives.

Working with the Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), whose leader Grzegorz Braun advocates closer ties with Russia and renewing the Nord Stream pipelines to take its gas to Europe, is a risk in a country where hostility to Moscow runs deep.

The 2022 Russian invasion of Poland's neighbour Ukraine rekindled fears of the Soviet troops who invaded Poland in 1939, and airspace incursions, including by three Russian missiles last week, have increased tension between Warsaw and Moscow.

But with around one in 10 Poles saying they would vote for the KKP - which has won support by vowing to support Polish farmers and send Ukrainian refugees back home - some right-wing leaders want to cooperate with it.

Surveys show the ruling pro-European coalition and the four right-wing opposition parties in a close race, one which former ruling nationalists Law and Justice (PiS) would have no chance of winning alone.

Tusk's Civic Coalition (KO) came out ahead in an IBRiS poll for Rzeczpospolita daily published this month, with 29%. Its partners in government, the Left, were on 7.6%, while other centrist allies came below the 5% threshold needed to enter parliament, leaving it well short of a majority.

PiS was on 16.5%. The party denies allegations from Tusk and Poland's European Union allies of undermining the independence of the judiciary during its eight-year rule to 2023.

The far-right Confederation, which expelled Braun in 2025 after he decided to run against its official candidate and co-leader Slawomir Mentzen in the presidential election, scored 13.2%, while the KKP had 10.5%.

"We will work toward having one single, big list (for the parliamentary elections)," PiS leader Jaroslaw Kaczynski said during an Independence Day march this month, adding that he would reach out to the KKP and Confederation.

Kaczynski had previously ruled out any cooperation with Braun, who is widely accused of being antisemitic, put out Hanukkah candles in parliament with a fire extinguisher, and who faces criminal charges of Holocaust denial. Braun has not pleaded guilty to the charges but has not retracted his comments.

He has remained silent on Kaczynski's proposal, but Confederation co-leader Krzysztof Bosak quickly ruled out forming a single list with PiS.

One-time PiS prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki, meanwhile, said his more moderate Development Plus would run alone and was scathing about Braun: "No coalitions with pro-Russian populists!" he wrote on X.

Nevertheless, analysts say that if cooperation with Braun is the price to pay for getting rid of Tusk, many on the right will be ready to accept it.

"If there is a chance at some point thanks to Grzegorz Braun that Donald Tusk will not be the prime minister again... I think that obviously it's possible," said Krzysztof Izdebski, director for advocacy and development at the Stefan Batory Foundation.

A NEW LEADER ON THE RIGHT?

Dealing with Braun is not the only stumbling block for parties that share conservative social views but differ on the economy and the role of the state.

For many conservatives the man who can unite the right is President Karol Nawrocki, the tough-talking, Trump-endorsed historian who came from relative obscurity to become head of state in 2025.

Tusk has cited Nawrocki's role in stymieing his agenda with vetoes in acknowledging that his government has not delivered on all its promises - a factor that has dented its support.

A savvy social media operator who has posted pictures of himself in the ring with boxing legend Manny Pacquiao and in the Oval Office with US President Donald Trump, Nawrocki has not been a member of any party, but analysts say he appeals to a wide range of conservatives.

"He acts as the builder of a big tent under which all centre-right parties can gather," PiS lawmaker Przemyslaw Czarnek, the party's favoured candidate for prime minister, told Reuters.

Czarnek said he could work with some KKP politicians, but would not cooperate with antisemites or "agents of Putin".

However, he told private broadcaster Radio Zet on Tuesday he couldn't imagine excluding Braun from any pact between right-wing parties in the upper house of parliament.

Nawrocki, who is subject to a Russian arrest warrant for his role in removing Red Army monuments in Poland, told Rzeczpospolita last month that the KKP "must be recognised as a presence in Polish politics".

Rafal Chwedoruk, a political scientist at Warsaw University, said that despite the KKP's current strong showing in the polls it was unlikely to get a seat at the cabinet table.

"At most - should the right-wing win - we might see a minority government tolerated by Braun; that is, one where he does not formally join the coalition, but instead receives certain political concessions in exchange for his support," he said.

data.title: Circio reports major new milestones achieved for circVec heart and eye gene therapy programs in Q4 R&D webcast
data.description:
• For the first time, data shows circVec advantage in combination with novel engineered AAV capsids targeting heart and eye, enabling a novel, highly targeted, next generation circVec gene therapy platform
  • AAV-circVec performance validated in human heart organoids in vitro, supporting translatability of the strong results in mouse models to future clinical studies
  • High business development activity with several gene and cell therapy R&D collaborations added during 2H 2026, including with Solid Biosciences
  • Preparations ongoing to initiate AAV-circVec testing in NHPs

Oslo, Norway, 27 November 2026 – Circio Holding ASA (OSE: CRNA), a biotechnology company developing novel circular RNA expression technology for gene and cell therapy, today presents new major pre-clinical milestones from its circVec heart and eye gene therapy programs in the Q4 R&D webcast at 10:00am CET.

Circio has tested the performance of its lead platform circVec in two engineered AAV capsids, one targeting the heart and one the eye. The capsid determines which specific tissue the vector reaches, whilst circVec determines how much protein is produced in the targeted cells. It is expected that these complementary strategies can establish a foundation for next generation AAV gene therapies that have specificity and potency levels that are unprecedented in the industry to date.

For the heart capsid, Circio’s circVec 3.2 demonstrates a significant advantage over the equivalent mRNA-based targeted AAV (AAV-mVec), with high signal specificity for cardiac tissue following systemic delivery. For the eye capsid, locally delivered circVec 4.0 shows a clear increase vs. the equivalent AAV-mVec. These results confirm, for the first time, that circVec can be combined with state-of-the-art engineered AAV capsids for both local and systemic delivery, and still deliver significant gene expression benefits. The findings are currently being explored further in follow-up studies with circVec generation 5, as well as in additional heart, eye and CNS-targeted capsids, to identify the most potent capsid and circVec combination.

In parallel, AAV-circVec has been validated in 2D heart organoids made from human iPSCs. circVec 3.2 shows up to 600-fold higher gene expression vs. benchmark AAV-mVec. Human cardiomyocyte organoids are a close in vitro model of human heart tissue. Importantly, the result demonstrates that the advantage measured in mouse heart is reproducible, and potentially superior, in human cells. This is critical evidence that the circVec expression advantage applies across different species, thereby lowering the translational risk Circio carries into disease models, non-human primate (NHP) studies and future clinical development.

“Gene therapies need to be both precise and potent, but current approaches often fall short of this goal. Circio has now produced clear in vivo evidence that circVec can substantially boost both conventional and engineered AAV capsids, and we are not aware of any directly competing expression technologies. In Circio´s view, circVec is therefore uniquely positioned to become a go-to technology to boost next generation AAV gene therapy,” said Dr. Thomas B Hansen, CTO of Circio. “The in vitro data from human heart organoids further strengthens our confidence that the promising findings in mouse readily translate to humans. This is a critical de-risking milestone and an important step forward on Circio´s journey to develop novel circVec-based gene therapies for patients with high unmet medical need.”

Circio is continuing to execute its business development strategy to broadly test circVec in a portfolio of strategic R&D collaborations. circVec is currently being trialed in several gene and cell therapy settings both internally and externally, including ongoing in vivo testing for the previously announced collaboration with a top 5 global pharma company. Looking ahead to 2027, the most promising collaborations are expected to progress to therapeutic and disease-relevant testing. In parallel, Circio aims to validate the AAV-circVec platform in larger animals, including pig and NHPs, with initial studies expected to start in Q2 2027 and first data in the second half of 2027.

The new results will be presented in detail by Circio´s CTO Dr. Thomas B Hansen in the live webcast today, Friday 27 November 2026 at 10:00am CET, together with a BD and corporate update from CEO Dr. Erik D Wiklund.

data.title: WiseTech Global Oct. CargoWise Revenue Rises, Says Confident To Meet FY27 Targets; Shares Climb
data.description:
CANBERA (dpa-AFX) - WiseTech Global Limited (WTC.AX), a provider of software solutions and logistics executions, Friday announced that it is confident to achieve fiscal 2027 targets based on performance to the end of October, and subject to the momentum and continuing favorable market conditions.

In its trading update, the company said year-to-date October CargoWise revenue grew 11%, driven by higher transaction volumes, growth from LGFF and STL price increases. Costs are tracking in line with expectations.

Following the news, the shares gained around 15% in Australian trading on Friday, closing at A$53.87.

For the full year, the company continues to expect underlying EBITDA range of $725 million to $780 million and revenue of $1.48 billion to $1.5 billion. Underlying EBITDA margin would be 49% to 51%, a growth of 3 to 5 percentage points year-over-year.

The annual outlook reflects underlying EBITDA growth ranging from 12 percent to 21 percent over a year ago, and revenue growth of 6 percent to 10 percent over prior year.

WiseTech noted that in August, its revenue guidance was predicated on modest adoption of key initiatives to achieve the bottom of guidance range, with those key initiatives second half weighted.

The company said the outlook confirmation is even before the adoption of the growth initiatives announced earlier.

WiseTech said it enter fiscal 2027 with a number of important goals that are tied to long-term strategy and vision, and that respond to the opportunities in the disruption currently seeing in the software sector generally from advancements in AI.

The company also said that it entered the new year with more growth opportunities across the business than ever before, a lower cost base, stronger margins, strong cash flow and a deleveraging plan that is ahead of schedule.

Further, AI Transformation delivered about $51 million of annualized EBITDA run-rate savings in fiscal 2026, and the firm expects a further $40 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of fiscal 2027, with net savings of $10 million in the year.

Regarding the adoption of AI, the company said more than 90% of its code is now written or assisted by AI. Engineering productivity is up 57%, compared with 45% at the end of fiscal 2026.

AI, and its impact on the operating models of WiseTech and customers, has been an important part of the Company's strategy since 2022, the firm said.

data.title: Asian stocks jump on U.S. futures rally, China profit beats, shrugging off tariff risks
data.description:
Asian equity markets traded higher on Friday, buoyed by a strong rally in U.S. stock futures ahead of Wall Street’s shortened post-Thanksgiving session. Renewed momentum in the artificial intelligence trade, sparked by late-Wednesday dip-buying, helped lift sentiment across the region.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 climbed 2.12% to above 58,700.00, with the Japanese yen . South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI jumped 4.23% to 4,910.47. Meanwhile, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index () up 2.05% to 22,685.50, and mainland China’s Shanghai Composite () rose 2.95% to 3,576.45, while the Shenzhen Component rose 4.86% to 10,573.03. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 () rose 0.80% to 8,833.60. The Australian dollar rose toward $0.67, climbing off a one-year low.

On the macroeconomic front, Beijing rejected U.S. allegations of industrial "overcapacity" as a "false premise" and vowed to defend its interests, as it faces a 20% U.S. tariff that could rise to 40% if Washington deems trade efforts insufficient. Supporting domestic sentiment, however, data showed Chinese industrial profits rose 16.0% Y/Y to CNY 6.74T in the first ten months of 2026, accelerating from 15.5% growth in the January–September period.

Core consumer prices in Tokyo’s central wards increased 2.9% Y/Y in November 2026, up from 2.6% in October, though slightly below the 3.0% consensus forecast.

Australia’s Canberra’s new Domestic Gas Reservation Scheme, requiring LNG exporters to reserve up to 20% of exports for domestic supply starting January 2028, bolstered expectations for lower energy costs.

In commodities, gold prices climbed above $3,600 an ounce, while crude oil climbed above $85 per barrel.

U.S. stock futures jumped on Friday as markets reopened following the Thanksgiving holiday, with markets looking to build on the pre-holiday dip-buying that emerged late Wednesday amid renewed strength in the artificial intelligence trade.

data.title: Coforge shares rebound 3.5% after Advent International dismisses speculation over imminent stake sale
data.description:
Shares of Coforge Ltd rose 3.5 percent to Rs 2,070 in morning trade on Friday, November 27, recovering their previous session's losses after private equity firm Advent International dismissed speculation over an imminent stake sale in the IT services company.

Coforge shares had plunged around 6 percent in intraday trade on Thursday to hit a nearly one-month low of Rs 1,945.6 after a media report said entities owned by Advent International were looking to offload around 10 percent stake in the company through block deals. The stock subsequently recovered some of its losses to settle 2.91 percent lower at Rs 2,000 on Thursday.

No block deal in Coforge shares had been reported as of Friday morning.

Advent International dismisses stake sale speculation

CNBC-TV18 reported on Thursday, citing unidentified sources, that entities owned by Advent International were likely to sell around 10 percent stake in Coforge through block deals to institutional investors. Two investment banks had reportedly been appointed to manage the proposed transaction, which was expected to take place soon.

  • Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today

However, Advent International later clarified that it remained a committed and active shareholder in Coforge. The US-based private equity firm also termed the speculation regarding imminent block trade transactions in the IT services company as unfounded.

Entities owned by Advent International currently hold around 20 percent stake in Coforge. At the company's current market capitalisation of around Rs 91,700 crore, a 10 percent stake would be valued at approximately Rs 9,170 crore.

Advent's share lock-in period to expire on November 30

The speculation over a potential stake sale comes ahead of the expiry of the mandatory six-month lock-in period on Advent International's shares in Coforge on November 30. Coforge had allotted the shares to Advent International on a preferential basis at Rs 1,815.91 apiece in April. The allotment followed the IT services company's announcement in December 2025 that it would acquire Encora at an enterprise value of $2.35 billion.

At Friday's prevailing market price, Coforge shares were trading around 14 percent above the preferential allotment price.

While the expiry of the lock-in period would enable Advent International to sell its shares, it does not necessarily imply an immediate stake dilution.

Coforge share price performance

Coforge shares have gained around 25 percent so far in 2026, significantly outperforming the benchmark Nifty 50, which has declined around 1.1 percent during the same period. Friday's rebound has also taken the stock marginally above Wednesday's closing price of Rs 2,060, erasing the losses triggered by the stake sale report.

data.title: Shares bounce after bruising month, dollar on course for third monthly gain
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nikkei up 2.1%, Nasdaq futures climb 2.4%
  • Chinese stocks jump almost 4% on new support measures
  • Dollar set for 1.7% monthly gain against major peers

By Stella Qiu

Asian shares steadied on Friday as they neared the end of a bruising month with a holiday lull giving some respite from AI jitters, while the dollar rode a wave of safe-haven demand and rate hike bets towards a third month of gains.

Wall Street shut on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday, but Nasdaq futures rallied 2.4% and S&P 500 futures were 1.7% higher. European bourses are set to extend the rally, with benchmark stock futures up 0.7%.

Japan's Nikkei jumped 2.1%, bringing to 4% its gains for the week, as it clawed back some of its 7.2% loss over the month.

Friday data showed core inflation in Tokyo hit a 16-month high in November, bolstering the case for an interest rate hike from the Bank of Japan as soon as next month.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MIAPJ0000PUS) jumped 1.7% to end the week 1.6% higher, but was still down 7.2% for the month.

Shares in South Korea surged 4% and China's blue chips gained 3.8% a day after hitting their lowest since June 2025, as the cabinet rolled out more support for capital markets.

"It is quite possible that the rebound could go further," said Shane Oliver, chief economist at AMP.

He cited factors such as the return of Jensen Huang to chipmaker Nvidia, the resilient US economy, strong corporate profit growth and December being a seasonally stronger period for shares.

"However, the risk of a deeper correction at some point in the next six months remains high."

However, Nvidia stayed a source of unease after S&P put its credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade.

The company told manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers containing its chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, the Financial Times said.

Elsewhere in tech, Elon Musk promised every US child two shares in his space and AI company SpaceX , for a total gift worth about $18 billion.

Oil prices were headed for the first weekly rise in four on renewed concerns about supply disruptions. Brent crude futures rose 0.3% on Friday to $96.85 a barrel, and were up 4.6% for the week. For the month, they were down nearly 18%.

DOLLAR REIGNS

The US dollar was headed for its third monthly gain on Friday, up 1.7% against major peers at 103.8, supported by expectations that the Federal Reserve is almost certain to lift interest rates in December, as well as safe-haven flows from an equities selloff.

Futures imply a 99% chance the Fed will raise rates by 25 basis points in December, but speculation of a half-point increase has faded. (0#USDIRPR)

The euro was up 0.1% at $1.0980 after news that Spanish central banking veteran Pablo Hernández de Cos would become the next president of the European Central Bank, a well-telegraphed move that suggested policy continuity.

The kiwi edged up 0.4% to $0.5482 after New Zealand's ruling centre-right coalition fell short of a parliamentary majority, som that it will have to resort to talks with the centrist Opportunity Party to retain power.

Bond investors are wondering if this month's broad losses in global stocks, coupled with doubts about the durability of AI-driven business investment, might make central banks less hawkish.

"The Fed could, of course, still blink," said David Rees, chief economist at Schroders. "But a Fed put would not necessarily be unambiguously positive for markets."

"If growth and inflation data remain firm, in a game of cat and mouse markets could soon begin pricing a more hawkish Fed back in, potentially setting off the same chain of events all over again."

The stocks rally drove down Treasuries, with two-year yields (US2YT=RR) rising 5 basis points to 4.6891% as the cash market reopened after the US holiday. They were up 8 bps this week.

Benchmark 10-year Treasury yields rose 7 bps to 4.9156%, but were flat at 2 bps for the week.
